outcome: One correlated incident timeline across firewall, endpoint and infrastructure telemetry, built on the fabric already in place.
overview: An energy operator usually has plenty of security telemetry and no single place to read it: firewalls report to one console, endpoints to another, and the correlation happens in an analyst’s head at three in the morning. FortiSIEM with FortiAnalyzer collects those sources into one timeline and correlates across them, so a sequence that looks unremarkable in each console individually becomes a single incident. Where the estate is already Fortinet, the integration effort that usually consumes a SIEM programme is largely done. What still has to be earned is detection content that fits this estate rather than a generic library.

benefits.text: Events from network, endpoint and infrastructure sources are correlated on one timeline
benefits.limits: Correlation only reaches sources that are actually onboarded; the log-source inventory, not the platform, sets the ceiling

benefits.text: Onboarding effort is lower where the estate already uses the same vendor’s fabric
benefits.limits: The saving is in parsing and integration, not in tuning; detection content still has to be written and maintained for this estate

benefits.text: An incident can be described from evidence rather than reconstructed across consoles
benefits.limits: Retention cost scales with ingest, so a coverage gain and a cost increase arrive together; the design has to state which sources are worth which retention rather than collecting everything by default

residency: Collectors and the event store run inside the operator’s own data centre, so security telemetry never leaves the jurisdiction — which is the usual constraint in this sector

notFor.situation: An operator already running a SIEM with tuned content and a staffed triage function
notFor.why: Replacing a tuned platform means rebuilding the content, and content is where the value accumulated

notFor.situation: An estate with no capacity to act on alerts out of hours
notFor.why: A platform that detects into an empty room converts a visibility problem into an evidence problem

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 12–16 weeks to a correlating platform with a first tuned content tranche
Support model: Vendor support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed tuning with an agreed alert-quality target.
1) Assessment — source inventory with volumes, retention obligations, current alert and incident statistics
2) Design — collector topology, per-source retention, content tranches and the alert-quality threshold
3) Build — supervisor, collectors, storage and the agreed source onboarding
4) Tune and hand over — content tranches enabled against the threshold, operations handed over
deliverables: An incident presents as one case with its contributing events, not as separate alerts
Each onboarded source has a stated retention period and the storage to honour it
A content tranche is only promoted once its false-positive rate is inside the agreed threshold

languages: English delivery; Arabic operational handover on request
